all_quotes.quote: The DCN emission is peaked on the TW Hya stellar position and spatially compact, barely resolved with the ALMA beam.
In contrast to DCO$^+$, which shows an increasing column density with radius, DCN is better fit by a model that is centrally peaked.
Deuterium fractionation appears to be efficient at a range of temperatures in this protoplanetary disk.
newly released ALMA science verification data on DCN 3-2 towards TW Hydrae have higher signal-to-noise and allow for significant constraints
Having dismissed dynamics, photochemistry, and mechanisms requiring grains, as plausible routes to significant deuterium fractionation in the outer disk
A more detailed characterization of the shape of the DCN radial profile requires higher spatial resolution than currently available.
